posts.title: Why SIPs Work
posts.excerpt: A short look at rupee cost averaging and why consistency matters more than timing.
posts.body_markdown:
## The core idea

Investing a fixed amount every month means you buy more units when prices are low and fewer when they are high. Over a long enough period this averages out your purchase cost without requiring you to predict anything.

## Why timing is the hard part

Markets do not move in a straight line, and the best and worst days tend to cluster together. Missing a handful of strong days because you were waiting for a better entry point has historically cost more than simply staying invested.

> Consistency is easier to sustain than accuracy.

## What this does not do

Rupee cost averaging reduces the impact of volatility on your purchase price. It does not remove market risk, and it does not protect against a falling market. Fund selection, asset allocation and your own time horizon all still matter.

Scheme documents for every fund are published at [AMFI](https://www.amfiindia.com). Read them before investing.
